speaker: narrator
text: A hundred years ago, Abbot Sulmar rang the great bell against the storm. The sea answered.

speaker: narrator
text: Tonight the tide draws back for fourteen minutes.

speaker: narrator
text: Three lamps wait in the dark. Light them, and the abbey may finally sleep.

speaker: narrator
text: You climb the sea stair with dry boots. Below you, for the first time in a hundred years, the abbey sleeps.

speaker: narrator
text: The tide caught you on the stair and you came home soaked to the collar. But the lamps hold, and the abbey sleeps.

speaker: warden
text: In, all of you. The sea takes the doorways first.

speaker: warden
text: Behind me. All of you. Yes, you too.

speaker: warden
text: Steady. I have seen worse weather.

speaker: warden
text: My knees remember these stairs.

speaker: warden
text: A gatekeeper. I know the type.

speaker: warden
text: Mind the little ones. They nip.

speaker: warden
text: When that bell swings, find a pillar.

speaker: warden
text: Now that is a proper harbour light.

speaker: warden
text: Hold the line. We will fetch them after.

speaker: warden
text: Water is coming in. Pick up your feet.

speaker: mender
text: Stay close to the light.

speaker: mender
text: Hold still. This only stings if you argue.

speaker: mender
text: They were brothers once. Be gentle.

speaker: mender
text: Brother Krogg. We have come to relieve you.

speaker: mender
text: She is still nursing them. Oh, Sister.

speaker: mender
text: Father Abbot. You can stop ringing now.

speaker: mender
text: One more light against the dark.

speaker: mender
text: There. Rest now.

speaker: mender
text: No, no, no. Up you get!

speaker: mender
text: The tide is turning. I can hear it.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: The sea takes. It also gives back, if you ask nicely.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: Kelp does not hurry. Neither do I.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: Smells like low tide. Lovely.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: Poor lamb. Rusted to his post.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: A ward full of crabs. She would be mortified.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: He never could leave that rope alone.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: There. That will keep the damp off.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: Up, dear. The kelp has you.

speaker: bloomweaver
text: She is coming home, the sea. Quick now.

speaker: duelist
text: I am only here for the candlesticks.

speaker: duelist
text: Nobody mentioned they would still be home.

speaker: duelist
text: Is any of this silver?

speaker: duelist
text: Big keys. Must be a big lock.

speaker: duelist
text: I have robbed worse hospitals.

speaker: duelist
text: That bell would fetch a fortune. I am only saying.

speaker: duelist
text: ...Fine. It is a bit lovely.

speaker: duelist
text: I am not carrying anyone.

speaker: duelist
text: I cannot swim in these boots.

speaker: ranger
text: Mine.

speaker: ranger
text: Left one.

speaker: ranger
text: Quiet.

speaker: ranger
text: Big.

speaker: ranger
text: Too many legs.

speaker: ranger
text: Loud.

speaker: ranger
text: Good.

speaker: ranger
text: Get up.

speaker: ranger
text: Tide.

speaker: pyromancer
text: Sorry. Sorry! That one got away from me.

speaker: pyromancer
text: Six generations of candles and nobody mentioned this.

speaker: pyromancer
text: Is it meant to be this damp?

speaker: pyromancer
text: Excuse us! We have an appointment?

speaker: pyromancer
text: I am sure she is a very good nurse.

speaker: pyromancer
text: My great-great-grandfather made his candles.

speaker: pyromancer
text: Oh! It caught first time.

speaker: pyromancer
text: Was that my fault? That felt like my fault.

speaker: pyromancer
text: Wet wicks. This is my nightmare.
